mainTopic: The garden-reeds story and its challenges to רבא, the size limit of a garden (בית כור vs. forty סאה), ישעיהו at חזקיה's door, and the house of a neighbor who forgot the עירוב.
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a story. Based on רבא's ruling that a pavilion made a whole garden count as enclosed for living, the reeds around the garden were removed, and רבא's students gathered them up. The next day the students challenged רבא three times: from a ברייתא about a town walled before it was settled, from רב אסי's rule about privacy screens, and from רב הונא's rule about a מחיצה made for convenience. The ריש גלותא ended the story with a פסוק: they were wise to ruin but not to fix. The גמרא then returns to the משנה, where רבי אלעאי allows carrying even in a בית כור. רבי יוחנן shows that רבי אלעאי and חנניה both learn from one פסוק about a king's courtyard, and they differ only on how big a medium-sized town is. A side story explains that ישעיהו set up a ישיבה at the sick חזקיה's door, though the גמרא warns against copying this. Finally, רבי אלעאי's second tradition about a neighbor who forgot the עירוב is challenged by a משנה, and רב ששת's answer begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The reeds are removed and then collected
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא removes the reeds, relying on רבא's ruling. רבא's students רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע collect them so they cannot be put back.
steps.simpleTranslation: He removed them. רב פפא and רב הונא son of רב יהושע went after him and collected them.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues from before. The reeds are pulled out because רבא ruled they were not needed, and רבא's students gather them up behind him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had ruled that the pavilion makes the whole garden count as enclosed for living, so the reeds were unnecessary. The students collected the reeds so the old setup could not be restored. This put רבא's ruling firmly into practice, and that sets up the challenges that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: He pulled them out / removed them

phrases.english: He removed them (the reeds).
phrases.notes: Continues the story from the previous section; the reeds were seen as unnecessary based on רבא's ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa went
and Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua,
and collected them after him.
phrases.notes: They were רבא's students and wanted his ruling to stand firm.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁלְפִינְהוּ. אֲזַל רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story earlier, where רבא ruled that the pavilion makes the garden count as enclosed for living.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, the reeds were removed based on רבא's ruling that the whole garden counts as enclosed for living.

steps.title: רבינא brings a ברייתא about measuring from a town
steps.stepSummary: The next day רבינא challenges רבא with a ברייתא. For a new town, the תחום שבת is measured from where people live. For an old town, it is measured from the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next day רבינא challenged רבא: For a new town, we measure from its settled area. For an old town, we measure from its wall.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא begins a challenge against רבא by quoting a ברייתא. This step is setting up the challenge; the punchline comes in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that in some towns the wall 'counts' as the edge of the town, and in others it does not. The question is what makes a wall count. רבינא will use the ברייתא's answer to attack רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (from an authoritative source)

phrases.english: The next day, Ravina raised an objection to Rava:
A new town, we measure it from its settled area,
phrases.notes: The Shabbat boundary is measured from where people actually live.

phrases.english: and an old town, from its wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling that was just carried out in practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a dwelling built later makes the garden count as enclosed for living.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step only sets up the source. The attack is completed in step 4.

steps.title: The ברייתא defines new and old towns
steps.stepSummary: A new town had its wall built first and was settled afterward. An old town was settled first and walled afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a new town and what is an old town? A new town was walled first and settled later. An old town was settled first and walled later.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains what 'new' and 'old' mean. This definition is the key fact רבינא needs for his challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of events decides whether the wall counts. If people lived there first and then built a wall, the wall was built for living, so it counts. If the wall came first, it was not built for living, so it does not count.
steps.confusionAlert: The names can seem backwards. 'New' here does not mean recently built. It means the wall came before the people, so the wall does NOT count. 'Old' means the people came first, so the wall DOES count.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיזוֹ הִיא חֲדָשָׁה וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא יְשָׁנָה?
phrases.english: Which is 'new' and which is 'old'?
New: one that was walled and afterward settled.
Old: one that was settled and afterward walled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזוֹ הִיא חֲדָשָׁה וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא יְשָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא and defines its terms.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wall counts as built for living only if people were living there before the wall went up.

steps.title: The garden is like a town walled before it was settled
steps.stepSummary: רבינא argues that the garden was fenced first and only later had a dwelling built in it. So it is like a 'new town', and its fence should not count as enclosed for living.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this garden too is like one that was walled and only afterward settled!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא applies the ברייתא to רבא's case. He argues that רבא's ruling contradicts it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The garden's fence was built before the pavilion. The ברייתא shows that living there afterward does not turn an earlier wall into a wall 'for living'. So the later pavilion should not change the status of the garden.

phrases.english: And this (garden) too
phrases.notes: Referring to רבא's case of the garden with the pavilion.

phrases.english: is like one that was walled and afterward settled!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי נָמֵי כְּהוּקְּפָה וּלְבַסּוֹף יָשְׁבָה דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא's definition to the garden and completes רבינא's challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the later pavilion makes the garden count as הוקף לדירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows that when a wall comes first and living comes later, the wall does not count for living. The garden fits exactly that pattern.

steps.title: רב פפא: a fence made for privacy is not a real partition
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רבא from רב אסי. Screens put up by builders are not a real מחיצה because they are only for privacy. So the garden fence, built for privacy, should not count either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: But רב אסי said that builders' screens are not considered a partition. This shows that since it was made for privacy, it is not a partition. Here too, since the fence was made for privacy, it is not a partition.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a second challenge against רבא. He uses a ruling of רב אסי about temporary screens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's challenge was about the order of events. רב פפא's challenge is about the purpose of the fence. A fence built just for privacy, not for living, is not a real מחיצה at all. The garden fence was built for privacy, so it should not make the garden count as enclosed for living.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's ruling now faces two challenges. רבינא says a fence built before the living does not count. רב פפא says a fence built only for privacy does not count as a real מחיצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It is ironic that רב פפא, who just helped carry out רבא's ruling, is now the one challenging it. This shows the students' honest drive to test their teacher's ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
But didn't Rav Asi say
builders' screens are not called a partition,
phrases.notes: Temporary screens put up for shade or privacy.

phrases.english: this shows that since it was made for privacy —
it is not a partition.
Here too, since it (the garden fence) was made for privacy —
it is not a partition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא: וְהָאָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate challenge against the same ruling of רבא, adding to רבינא's challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the garden fence counts as enclosing the garden for living.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב אסי rules that a structure made only for privacy is not a real מחיצה. The garden fence was made for privacy, so it cannot count as a wall for living.

steps.title: A third challenge: a wall made for convenience is not a wall
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע challenges רבא with רב הונא's rule that a מחיצה made for convenience does not count as a מחיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא the son of רב יהושע said to רבא: But didn't רב הונא say that a partition made for convenience is not called a partition?
steps.whatsHappening: Another student attacks רבא's ruling. He quotes רב הונא's rule that a fence built only for comfort or convenience does not count as a real wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא let them remove the reeds because he held the garden fence was already good enough. But that fence was built to guard or ease the use of the garden, not to enclose a living space. Under רב הונא's rule it would not count, so the reeds were needed after all.

keyTerms.meaning: A partition or wall that legally encloses an area
Made for convenience or ease, not to enclose a living area
It is not called a partition (halachically it does not count)
'But didn't [so-and-so] say…?' A formula for bringing a challenge

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: And Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said to Rava:
But didn't Rav Huna say:
a partition made for convenience
is not called a partition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the third challenge in a row against רבא, parallel to רב פפא's challenge from רב אסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the garden's fence was enough, so the reeds could be removed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A fence built for convenience is not a real מחיצה. The garden fence is that kind of fence, so the garden was not properly enclosed.

steps.title: רב הונא's rule in practice: the cattle troughs of מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה made a separate עירוב for each row of houses in מחוזא, because the cattle troughs did not count as a real wall. This shows the rule in action.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבה בר אבוה made an עירוב for all of מחוזא row by row, because of the cattle troughs. And cattle troughs are like a partition made for convenience.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב הונא's rule with a real-life example. רבה בר אבוה did not rely on the cattle troughs as a wall, so he made a separate עירוב for each row of houses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cattle troughs were built for feeding animals, which is a convenience use. So they could not join the town into one enclosed area. This proves that a structure built for convenience is not a מחיצה, which makes the challenge against רבא stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes an עירוב (joins areas so one may carry between them)
Row by row (each row of houses separately)
Cattle troughs or ditches where the oxen feed
מחוזא, a large Jewish town in Babylonia

phrases.english: For Rabba bar Avuh
made an eiruv for all of Meḥoza
row by row
because of the cattle troughs.
And the cattle troughs
are like a partition made for convenience.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב הונא's rule quoted in step 6 with the practice of רבה בר אבוה in מחוזא. This strengthens רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's challenge against רבא.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's rule that a מחיצה made for convenience is not a מחיצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבה בר אבוה, who made a separate עירוב for each row in מחוזא and did not rely on the cattle troughs

steps.title: The ריש גלותא's verdict: wise to ruin, not to fix
steps.stepSummary: The ריש גלותא quotes a פסוק about the rabbis: they knew how to undo the arrangement but did not know how to do good.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ריש גלותא read about them: 'They are wise to do harm, but to do good they do not know.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. The ריש גלותא sums it up with a sharp פסוק from ירמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On Friday they took away the reeds that made carrying in the garden permitted. On שבת, all their learning only proved that the reeds had been needed. In the end, carrying in the garden was forbidden, so their cleverness only caused a loss.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, the political head of Babylonian Jewry

steps.whatToRemember: The three challenges (from רבינא, רב פפא, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע) were left unanswered. The garden fence did not make the garden a properly enclosed living area, so removing the reeds was a mistake.

phrases.english: The Exilarch recited about them:
"They are wise to do evil,
but to do good they do not know."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story by judging the result of all the challenges.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenges stand. The reeds had been needed, and taking them down left the garden forbidden for carrying.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי אלעאי allows even a בית כור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. רבי אלעאי heard from רבי אליעזר that one may carry even in a garden the size of a בית כור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעאי said: I heard from רבי אליעזר: even a בית כור.
steps.whatsHappening: The story is over, and the גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה. This line sets up the comment that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual limit for carrying in a garden or קרפף is a בית סאתים. רבי אלעאי reports a much bigger limit in the name of רבי אליעזר: a בית כור, which is thirty בית סאה. The next step will compare this size with another opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: I heard (a tradition passed down from a teacher)
An area where a כור of seed is sown, equal to thirty בית סאה

phrases.english: Rabbi Elai said,
I heard from Rabbi Eliezer:
even a beit kor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעַאי, שָׁמַעְתִּי מֵרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The גמרא returns to the משנה after finishing the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר's tradition, carrying is permitted in a garden even as large as a בית כור.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow חנניה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה's view is not like חנניה. A ברייתא quotes חנניה, who allows even forty, like a king's courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like חנניה. As it was taught: חנניה says: even if it is forty סאה, like the courtyard of a king.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short note. רבי אלעאי's size of a בית כור is not the same as חנניה's view, which a ברייתא quotes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנניה gives a different, larger size: forty בית סאה, compared to a king's courtyard. A בית כור is thirty בית סאה. So the משנה's tradition sets a different limit and cannot be matched with חנניה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
The courtyard or grounds of a king

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not like חנניה' means the two give different size limits. רבי אלעאי's בית כור is thirty בית סאה, and חנניה allows forty. So they cannot be the same opinion, and the משנה's tradition is the smaller, stricter limit of the two.

phrases.english: Our mishna is not in accordance with Ḥananya.
As it was taught, Ḥananya says:
even if it is forty se'a
like the courtyard of a king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains whose view the משנה's line matches by comparing it with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעאי's tradition of a בית כור is a separate view from חנניה's, which allows forty, like a king's courtyard.

steps.title: Both opinions come from one verse about a royal courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that רבי אלעאי and חנניה both learned their view from the פסוק about ישעיהו and the 'middle courtyard.' The word is written 'city' but read 'courtyard,' which teaches that royal courts were as big as medium-sized towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Both of them learned their view from the same פסוק: 'And ישעיהו had not yet gone out of the middle courtyard.' The פסוק is written 'the city' but we read it 'courtyard.' From here we learn that royal courts were like medium-sized towns.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains where the two opinions from the last step come from. They both use one פסוק, which shows that a king's courtyard was as big as a medium-sized town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is written one way (כתיב: 'the city') and read another way (קרי: 'courtyard'). The two words together teach that this courtyard was the size of a town. Both רבי אלעאי and חנניה agree on this source. That sets up the next question: if they agree on the source, what do they actually disagree about?

keyTerms.meaning: It is written one way and we read it another way (כתיב and קרי)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the two תנאים argue about the פסוק. They both accept the same פסוק. Their argument is only about how big a 'medium-sized town' is.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Both of them expounded one verse,
as it is said: 'And it was, Isaiah'
had not gone out to the middle courtyard'
It is written 'the city' and we read 'courtyard'
From here we learn about the royal courts
that they were like medium-sized towns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the shared scriptural source for the two opinions quoted in steps 9-10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A king's courtyard was the size of a medium-sized town, as learned from the כתיב/קרי of 'city' and 'courtyard.'

steps.title: What exactly do they disagree about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if both use the same פסוק, what is the point of their disagreement?
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step. If both learned from the same פסוק, where do they actually differ?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree that a royal courtyard was like a medium-sized town. One still allows a בית כור and the other allows forty סאה. So the disagreement must be somewhere else, and the גמרא wants to find it.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how two different rulings can come from the one shared source given in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact point of disagreement between רבי אלעאי and חנניה.

steps.title: They disagree about the size of a medium town
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעאי holds that a medium-sized town is a בית כור. חנניה holds that it is forty סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds that medium-sized towns are a בית כור. The other Sage holds that they are forty סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The argument is only about how big a 'medium-sized town' is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the royal courtyard was like a medium-sized town. רבי אלעאי says such a town is a בית כור (thirty סאה). חנניה says it is forty סאה. That is why each allows carrying in a different size of enclosed area.

keyTerms.meaning: An area where a כור (30 סאה) of seed is planted
An area for forty סאה of seed

steps.whatToRemember: Same source, different measurement. רבי אלעאי says a בית כור, and חנניה says forty סאה. Each sets the size of a medium town, which is the size of the royal courtyard.

phrases.english: One Sage holds: medium-sized towns
are a בית כור.
And the other Sage holds: they are forty סאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר עֲיָירוֹת בֵּינוֹנִיּוֹת הָוְיָין בֵּית כּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about the size of a medium-sized town: a בית כור or forty סאה.

steps.title: Why was ישעיהו in the middle courtyard?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a side question about the story in the פסוק: what was ישעיהו doing there?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what was ישעיהו doing there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the story in the פסוק. This sets up a short aggadic section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה part is finished. The גמרא now wants to know why a נביא was sitting in the king's middle courtyard.

phrases.english: And what was Isaiah doing there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the הלכה and asks about the story in the פסוק quoted in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason ישעיהו was in the king's middle courtyard.

steps.title: ישעיהו set up a ישיבה at the sick king's door
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן: חזקיה was sick, so ישעיהו set up a ישיבה at his door.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This teaches that חזקיה was sick. ישעיהו went and set up a ישיבה at his door.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why ישעיהו was there. He set up Torah learning at the door of the sick king חזקיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the merit of Torah learning near a sick person helps him heal. That is why ישעיהו was in the courtyard next to the king's room.

keyTerms.meaning: He set up a ישיבה (a group of Torah learners)

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
This teaches that Hezekiah was sick,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָלַךְ יְשַׁעְיָהוּ וְהוֹשִׁיב יְשִׁיבָה עַל פִּתְחוֹ.
phrases.english: and Isaiah went and set up a yeshiva at his door.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ישעיהו set up a ישיבה at the door of the sick חזקיה.

steps.title: Learning a practice for a sick Torah scholar
steps.stepSummary: From the story, someone learns that when a תלמיד חכם is sick, people should set up a ישיבה at his door.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here we learn that when a תלמיד חכם is sick, we set up a ישיבה at his door.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a practical lesson from the story about ישעיהו and חזקיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ישעיהו did this for חזקיה, maybe we should do the same for any sick Torah scholar. This lesson is about to be questioned in the next step.

phrases.english: From here we learn about a Torah scholar who became sick,
that we set up a yeshiva at his door.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical lesson from the story in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should set up a ישיבה at the door of a sick תלמיד חכם.

steps.title: The practice is rejected because it may stir up the שטן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this lesson. Doing this might stir up the שטן against the sick person.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is not a proper thing to do, because perhaps it will provoke the שטן against him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the lesson from the last step and says we should not do this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drawing a lot of attention to the sick person's merits could cause the שטן to accuse him, and that could make things worse. So the story about ישעיהו does not become a general practice for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a proper thing / not correct
To provoke the שטן against him

steps.whatToRemember: The story shows ישעיהו set up a ישיבה for חזקיה. The גמרא still says this is not a general practice, because it might stir up the שטן against the sick person.

phrases.english: But this is not a proper thing,
since perhaps it will come to provoke the Satan against him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the practical lesson drawn in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects turning the story into a general practice. It does not reject the story itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Setting up a ישיבה at the door might provoke the שטן to accuse the sick person and make him worse.

steps.title: Second tradition: the house of the one who forgot the עירוב is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעאי reports another ruling he heard from רבי אליעזר. If one resident of a courtyard forgot to join the עירוב, his house is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I also heard from him: if one of the people of a courtyard forgot and did not make an עירוב, his house is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה, a second teaching that רבי אלעאי heard from רבי אליעזר. This one is about a neighbor who forgot to join the courtyard's עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Several families share one חצר. On שבת they may carry between their houses and the courtyard only if they all joined an עירוב. If one forgot, he gives up his share in the courtyard to the others. The ruling says 'his house is forbidden.' The simple meaning is that the house is forbidden to him alone, while the others may still carry into and out of it.

keyTerms.meaning: And I also heard from him, introducing another tradition from the same teacher (רבי אליעזר)
The residents who share one courtyard
A shared food arrangement that joins the residents' areas so they may carry on שבת
His house is forbidden, meaning no carrying between it and the courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: 'His house is forbidden' does not mean nobody may enter the house. It refers only to carrying objects between that house and the courtyard on שבת. The open question is whom the ban covers.

phrases.english: And I also heard from him:
phrases.notes: רבי אלעאי speaking about רבי אליעזר

phrases.english: residents of a courtyard, where one forgot
and did not join in the eiruv —
his house is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Implied: forbidden to him, but permitted to the others

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about ישעיהו and חזקיה, the גמרא returns to the משנה's list of רבי אלעאי's traditions and takes up the next one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one resident forgot to join the עירוב, his house is forbidden for carrying. The implication is that the ban applies to him alone, not to the other residents.

steps.title: A משנה says the house is forbidden to everyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling with a משנה stating that the forgetful neighbor's house is forbidden for carrying both to him and to the other residents.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in a משנה: his house is forbidden for taking out and bringing in, both for him and for them?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. Another משנה says the house is closed to everyone, not just to the one who forgot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעאי's tradition suggests only the forgetful neighbor is restricted. The משנה (in the sixth chapter of עירובין) adds the words 'לו ולהן,' meaning 'for him and for them,' so the others are restricted too. The two sources seem to disagree about whether the other residents may carry into and out of his house.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה? This introduces a challenge from a משנה
To carry out and to bring in
For him and for them, meaning both the one who forgot and the other residents

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishna:
his house is forbidden for taking out and bringing in
for him and for them?!
phrases.notes: The words 'for them' are the source of the difficulty

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of Step 18 with a contradicting משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of רבי אלעאי's tradition that the house is forbidden only to the one who forgot.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly says the house is forbidden 'for him and for them,' so the other residents are restricted as well. This contradicts the implied leniency for them.

steps.title: רב ששת begins the answer: there is no contradiction
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, quoting רב ששת, announces that the two sources do not really conflict. His explanation follows in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, the son of רב יהושע, said in the name of רב ששת: it is not difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer. רב ששת's view is introduced with the claim that there is no real contradiction, and the actual resolution comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'לא קשיא' signals that the answer will show the two sources are discussing different situations. So far we only know that רב ששת will reconcile them. How he does it has not yet been stated.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This opens an answer showing the sources do not truly conflict

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the full answer. It only announces that one is coming. Do not stop here and assume the contradiction has been resolved.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said
that Rav Sheshet said:
It is not difficult,
phrases.notes: The explanation continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the defense against the challenge raised in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reconciling the sources, most likely by showing they refer to different cases. The details have not yet appeared on this amud.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעאי's tradition and the משנה seem to disagree about whether the other residents are restricted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Still pending. רב ששת will explain how both sources can be correct.
